text:
marta_sales: Heads-up — HS Enterprise is asking if we can run a 30‑day on‑prem air‑gapped POC. They need a short feasibility summary for packaging, upgrade cadence, and security controls by EOD. They attached a security questionnaire (sending offline). Quick bullets I can send them: what we can do vs blockers?
lee_se: thanks — can you paste the top asks from their questionnaire? esp sections on signing, KMS/HSM, and expected upgrade rhythm.
marta_sales: main asks: 1) support for USB / optical bootstrap media, 2) signed bundles + SBOM, 3) ability to import customer HSM public key for verification, 4) delta updates w/ limited bandwidth, 5) offline activation window (30 days) and emergency hotfix path, 6) audit logs and offline telemetry opt‑out.
jonah_ops: short answer: feasible but with constraints. Notes:
- We produce immutable signed bundles (OCI tarball style) that can be distributed via USB or air‑gapped repo.
- Default bundle size ~2.5GB (full installer). We offer "mini" delta bundles that contain only changed artifacts; delta chain is supported within the same minor release (e.g., 1.4.x -> 1.4.y). Cross‑minor deltas not supported today.
- Offline activation: we have an activator CLI that can generate a time‑bound activation token. For fully airgapped installs, customer provides a CSR and we return a signed token; token validity is configurable but needs agreement (we usually do 14–30 days).
- Signing: bundles are signed with our build key. We can publish a customer‑consumable verification key and also accept a customer public key to embed in the verifier so they can verify locally.
- HSM: we can support BYO‑HSM for verification (public keys) but we do not run customer keys in our hosted sign pipeline. Key import and ceremony must be handled at customer side.
- Bandwidth: recommend delta bundles + resumable chunking (we break transfers into 64MB chunks).
(also: emoji :thumbsup:)
nina_security: a few security caveats to call out for the customer and legal: 
- SBOM: we can supply SPDX v2.2 SBOMs per bundle. For deepest assurance we need to freeze dependency versions before a signed release — otherwise SBOMs change between builds.
- Signing verification: we can ship a verification utility that verifies signatures and SBOM integrity offline. If customer requires on‑prem key material managed in an HSM, we accept an exported public key for verification; we do not accept external private keys in our build system.
- Certificate rotation: need to define a rotation cadence and emergency key‑revocation process (what happens if a signing key is compromised?). Add a clause to SOW.
- Questionnaire item: "Do you support FIPS 140‑2 HSM for signing?" Answer: verification can be done against public keys exported from a FIPS HSM; signing operations are performed by our build system using industry‑standard crypto (we can discuss attestation if required).
ashley_eng: operational recommendation from infra: for the POC pick a narrow image set and a single minor line (e.g., 2.1.x) to avoid delta complexity. We can produce a two‑tier payload: base bundle + daily micropatch deltas. Example commands for onboarding (to include in the runbook):
```
# verify bundle signatures offline
./rwd-verify --bundle /media/usb/release-2.1.5.tar.gz --pubkey customer-pub.pem
# activator (airgapped)
./rwd-activator --csr customer-install.csr --expires 2026-04-20 > activation.token
```
jonah_ops: small clarifier — the activator is an offline CLI we run in our professional services environment, or we can hand them a signed token if they prefer. For the POC we usually do: customer generates CSR -> hands to us (SFTP/USB) -> we return signed token. Document that the token verification code runs entirely on the node and requires no egress.
deploy-bot: build signed: release-2.1.5 (sha256: a3c9...f1b2) uploaded to staging-artifacts (signed by rwd-build-2026) :package:
marta_sales: perfect. two asks from me before I respond to the customer: 1) a one‑paragraph feasibility summary I can paste into the SOW/answer to the questionnaire, and 2) recommended default cadence (we prefer to propose quarterly minor upgrades + monthly micropatch deltas for POC).
lee_se: draft sentence: "Redwood can deliver signed, verifiable on‑prem bundles for isolated environments. We support USB and offline repo distribution, provide SPDX SBOMs and a local verification utility, and enable time‑bound activation tokens for air‑gapped installs. Delta updates are supported within a minor release; cross‑minor upgrades require a full bundle. We can accommodate customer‑provided HSM public keys for local verification; signing operations remain within Redwood's build pipeline. Recommended cadence: quarterly minor upgrades with monthly micropatch deltas for production; for the POC we recommend monthly deltas and one minor upgrade at the end of the trial."
nina_security: tweak: add sentence about key rotation and incident clause.
lee_se: updated: "... Signing operations remain within Redwood's build pipeline. Customer may import HSM‑backed public keys for local verification; a key rotation and emergency revocation process will be defined in the SOW."
marta_sales: this is great — I'm sending this to the customer now. Can we also get a short line on commercial constraints (e.g., min commit for dedicated upgrade frequency or extra PS hours)?
\onah_ops: quick: add estimated PS: 2 days of runbook + 1 day for package customization + 0.5 day for token exchanges = 3.5d standard. Add note: if customer asks for BYO signing (private key in our pipeline) that's not supported and will require a negotiated professional services arrangement and security review.
marta_sales: thanks all — I'll paste and keep you looped. :seedling:
